state_limits: Parent pin matches child HEAD. Tracked-only child status was clean; untracked and ignored paths were not enumerated. No real resume data was read and no agent command was executed.
description: A driver for repeated multi-persona document critique, score aggregation and a plateau stop condition, with a human applying accepted edits between rounds.
scope_audience: The intended user is someone iteratively improving a resume or document with an agent CLI that reads stdin and writes stdout. The tool does not itself edit the document or guarantee truthful reviewer judgments.

creativity.reason: Independent adversarial reviewer personas plus a trend-based stopping rule are an interesting workflow composition; comparisons to other critique loops were not searched.

current_usefulness.reason: The inspected driver runs reviewers, parses scores, aggregates rounds and stops on plateau, but no real agent interaction, reviewer accuracy or output record was verified.

expected_usefulness.reason: If the intended scope succeeds, a user can expose different document weaknesses and see whether revisions move rubric scores; those scores are not an objective quality measure.

impl_progress.reason: loop.py implements prompt/run/retry/aggregation/plateau control and README/RUBRIC define the contract, but there is no local test suite or recorded run inspected.

presentability.reason: README explains persona roles, workflow, commands and stop behavior; agent CLI and prompt-quality limits are made explicit.

delivery_likelihood.reason: The local driver is present, but useful output depends on an externally supplied agent command and reviewer quality; no run evidence was retained in the inspected root.

verification: README, loop.py flow and rubric contract; executed=false; No resume or personal document was opened; no external agent was launched; no score quality was assessed.

evidence.locator: lines 7-25, multi-reviewer workflow; lines 38-71, agent contract and stopping
lines 36-52, score parsing; lines 180-260, rounds, aggregation and plateau flow

contribution: A controlled human-in-the-loop critique cycle rather than a single score prompt: personas see a common text/rubric, results are aggregated, and the user decides which edits to accept. The scoring trend is a proxy, not proof of better hiring outcomes.
alternatives_question: Which document-review loops support independent persona critiques, exact quoted findings and human-selected edits across rounds, and how do they prevent score convergence from becoming rubric gaming?
reason: The driver is implemented and its bounded workflow is understandable, but agent quality, usefulness and score validity have no local result evidence.
next_step: Use a fictional document with known seeded defects, check whether each persona identifies its assigned issue with accurate quotations, and report score changes only as proxy observations.
